## A fish out of water

A multidisciplinary sport scientist

. . .

My usual audiences are...other people studying sport science and working in sport!

. . .

<br />
<br />

From the ANZIAM website:

> Our role is to...Provide for the exchange of ideas and information between applied mathematicians and [users of mathematics in science, engineering and industry]{.yellow}

. . .

<br />
<br />

My goal is to shed light on [how mathematics and statistics is used in sport]{.cyan} today, and perhaps entice you to work in this space in future!

## Growing into "awkward adolescence" {.smaller}

Technology changes:

- Video
- Wearable and portable technologies
- Count statistics to detailed event data (play-by-play)
- High-speed video
- Multi-camera OTS

Analytical practices:

- Notational analysis
- Programmatic approaches to working with data
- Accessibility of statistical modelling outside of academia
- Computer vision
- Integrating data from multiple sources (across disciplines)

Dedicated tertiary courses for sports analytics

Growth in private sports data and technology providers

Competitor behaviours

## Research projects: From counts to sequences

- Early days: Performance indicators using game action counts
     - Sampaio et al. https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/17461390600676200
- Progressing to: Play-by-play data, network analysis, sequences / chains of actions
     - Fewell et al., https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0047445
     - Taylor et al., Network analysis in AFL

## Research projects: Video analysis

- Early days: Manual notational analysis to derive new features
     - https://www.taylorfrancis.com/chapters/edit/10.4324/9781315776743-6/overview-development-notation-analysis-mike-hughes
- Progressing to: Computer vision
     - Hall et al. https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00521-020-05485-3

## Research projects: Positioning data (GPS / LPS)

- Early days: Understanding physical demands of training and competition
     - Physical demands in soccer: https://researchportal.murdoch.edu.au/esploro/outputs/journalArticle/The-physical-demands-of-professional-soccer/991005544546907891
- Progressing to: Spatiotemporal analyses to uncover tactical structures
     - Seakins et al. https://www.mdpi.com/1424-8220/23/10/4891
     - Raabe et al. https://doi.org/10.1080/02640414.2024.2414363

## Challenges and opportunities {.smaller}

Growth in sports analytics has been rapid but uneven

- Some sports / orgs have been faster to adapt / implement
- Resourcing differences between sports and organisations within sports

Sometimes growing in ways we're not quite ready for ("running before walking")

- E.g., focus on hiring data scientists / analytics specialists without understanding and investing in infrastructure and support functions upstream (IT, data engineering, data governance)
- Varying maturity in leaders' skills in using and interpreting data to inform their decisions

Role clarity and integration within a performance team

- Looking for the mix of domain, interpersonal, data and analytics, and computer science / programming skills
- Is analytics a distinct role? Is it better to upskill an SME? Is it just sport science with larger data sets?

Many rich sources of data across disciplines, although the industry generally lacks sufficient mathematical / statistical knowledge to analyse in sophisticated and robust ways -- opportunities for those with specialist skill sets to make an impact

Research and analysis of women's sport preparation and performance
